items.stem: Which word describes an event with probability 0?
items.answer: Impossible
items.markingKey: P = 0 means the event cannot happen.

items.stem: Explain why the probabilities of all the possible outcomes of an experiment add up to 1.
items.answer: One of the outcomes is certain to happen, and they cannot happen together, so their probabilities together give a certain event, probability 1.
items.markingKey: B1 one outcome certain; B1 mutually exclusive, total 1 [2]

items.stem: Explain what is meant by "outcomes are equally likely", using a fair dice.
items.answer: Each outcome has the same chance of happening; on a fair dice each number 1–6 has probability 1/6.

items.stem: Diego says: "Tomorrow it will either snow or not snow, so the probability that it snows is 1/2." Explain why Diego is wrong.
items.answer: The two outcomes are not equally likely, so the probability is not necessarily 1/2; it depends on the place and the season.
items.markingKey: B1 outcomes not equally likely; B1 context [2]

items.stem: Kwame rolls a dice and gets 5 sixes in a row. Kwame says a six is less likely on the next roll because "it is due to be something else". Explain why Kwame is wrong if the dice is fair.
items.answer: Each roll is independent; the dice has no memory, so P(six) is still 1/6 on the next roll.
